{{Short description|Student award of British university}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
The '''Thomas Bond Sprague Prize''' is a prize awarded annually to the student or students showing the greatest distinction in [[actuarial science]],  [[finance]], [[insurance]], [[operations research|mathematics of operational research]], [[probability theory|probability]], [[risk]] and [[statistics]] in the [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Master of Mathematics/Master of Advanced
Studies]] examinations of the [[University of Cambridge]], also known as Part III of the Mathematical Tripos.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/thomas-bond-sprague-prize-winners|title=Thomas Bond Sprague Prize-winners|accessdate=August 23, 2026}}</ref> The prize is named after [[Thomas Bond Sprague]], the only person to have been president of both the [[Institute of Actuaries]] in London and the [[Faculty of Actuaries]] in Edinburgh. It is awarded by the [[Rollo Davidson Prize|Rollo Davidson Trust]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/rollo-davidson-trust|title=Statistical Laboratory|accessdate=August 23, 2026}}</ref> of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]], following a donation by D. O. Forfar, MA, FFA, FRSE (alumnus of Trinity College, Cambridge), former Appointed [[Actuary]] of  [[Scottish Widows]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.theactuary.com/news/2012/08/social-news-round-up-august-2012/|title=Social news round-up - August 2012  &#124;  The Actuary, the official magazine of the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries|accessdate=July 30, 2019}}</ref>
